Problem Statement:
Carlos the famous building demolisher is employed by BitMagic Inc. They have given him a list of prices they can pay him for demolishing each building. There are N buildings that he needs to demolish so he has a list of N prices . Carlos instead of carrying on with his work of demolishing started exploring the mathematical properties of the the list of prices. He wanted to compute the bitwise xor ( "^" operator) for any contiguous subarray present in the list of prices.If the bitwise xor of the given subarray is greater than or equal to a given Z then he is "happy" or else he is "unhappy". Being very curious he also changes some prices to a desired price as and when he requires.

Carlos asks Q questions which can be either of the following:

1) Find xor of a subarray and check if it will make him happy or not

2) Modify an element to a given price

Help him find if he is happy or unhappy for the given question he asks.
input_spec:
The first line contains a single integer N denoting the number of buildings/number of prices
The second line contains the N integers - denoting the the prices being paid for each building
The next line contains a single integer Q denoting the number of questions Carlos asks
The next Q line can be either of the following:
1 x y : Change price for building x to y
2 x y z : Find subarray of the range [x,y] and compare it to Z
output_spec: For each question of type 2 output whether carlos is "happy" or "unhappy" in a single line
